label: Run 13 · all 3 chats
note: Every chat of run 13 (run 12 with the turn no longer fixed at one message from each): the same pair, the same brief and the same prompt, each written by a different writer. All of them were written improvisation by improvisation to the same instructions, under IMPROVISATIONS. What the instructions fix (how each improvisation goes, the traps, how interest moves) is shared by design and is not a template, and is not held against the set: list the improvisations it decides under excused and judge only what the writers made of it.

chat.variety.why: Setting aside what the instructions fix (the Denial lies, the Spiral narration and the agreed date at the end), the three chats still play almost the same night in the same order. Reuben opens with a top-hat compliment and a disclosure or lie. Brick answers with her own disclosure and either clocks his fast reply or hands him a time slot. Then come the Marguerite shared-calendar fights, the 'sometime' cab sob, and Delphine's 'one sentence'. Ali Wong's and Jimmy Carr's chats even share Brick's 'sixty seconds' ultimatum and the itemised itinerary as the come-on. Verbatim lines recur in more than two chats, and several pairs share whole jokes; each chat adds a few of its own (Ali's ring light and pigs-in-a-blanket, Jimmy's 'forbidden to be funny', Joel's plain statement of fear), which keeps this off a 1 but not far enough from one scene to reach a 3.
evidence: Four-second reply says you live here, handsome.
you replied in four seconds flat.
chat.variety.raise: Give each chat a different opening move and a different turning device (not the sixty-second ultimatum or the itinerary come-on every time), and stop reusing the 'dishwasher-safe' kanji, rosé-and-cocktail-sword and top-hat-at-home lines across chats.
